In pottery and porcelain clay bodies, additions of only 2% can produce marked improvements in workability and dry strength without much effect on fired color. The use of up to 5% is common, especially where high plasticity is needed in a white-burning body.

Bentonites have incredibly small particle sizes (larger surface areas). Combined with active surface chemistry that enhances water retention, bentonite becomes the most plastic and impermeable common clay material used in ceramics. Its contribution to working properties in glazes and clay bodies is balanced by its ability to improve firing characteristics, reducing cracking and warping during firing for superior finished products.
